text: When you build a REST API, good design makes it easy for others to use. Start with clear endpoints that describe your resources, such as /users or /orders. Use the correct HTTP methods and return proper status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is missing. Always write clear documentation so developers understand how your API works. Versioning is also important. If you change your API in a way that breaks existing code, create a new version, like /v2/users. This keeps old applications working while you improve your service. Following these practices helps your API stay reliable and simple to maintain.
